summary: Right-angled trigonometry (sin, cos, tan) relates a reference angle θ to a pair of sides. The two shorter sides are named RELATIVE TO θ — opposite is across from θ, adjacent is next to θ — while only the hypotenuse is fixed (opposite the right angle, longest side). The central danger is reducing trigonometry to mnemonic recitation (SOHCAHTOA) without understanding, so learners mislabel sides, pick the wrong ratio and cannot recover when a triangle is rotated or when they work from the other acute angle. Ground the ratios in similarity/ratio-invariance: for a fixed angle the within-triangle ratio (e.g. opposite÷hypotenuse) is constant across similar triangles, and that constant IS sin of the angle. Distinguish finding an unknown SIDE (rearrange the ratio) from finding an unknown ANGLE (apply the inverse function).
misconceptions: Labels opposite and adjacent relative to the RIGHT angle instead of the reference angle θ, so every ratio is set up wrong
Relies on the SOHCAHTOA mnemonic without understanding, and cannot choose which ratio applies when given a particular pair of sides
Mislabels the sides when the triangle is drawn rotated or in a non-standard orientation
For an unknown side, cannot rearrange the ratio to isolate it (e.g. leaves the unknown in the denominator)
For an unknown angle, forgets to use the inverse function (uses sin instead of sin⁻¹) or reports the ratio value as if it were the angle

activities.title: Labels that move with the reference angle
steps: Mark the reference angle θ FIRST on a right-angled triangle, then label 'opposite' (across from θ) and 'adjacent' (next to θ, and NOT the hypotenuse) relative to it.
Label the hypotenuse as the side opposite the right angle — the longest side, which stays fixed.
Now mark the OTHER acute angle as θ on the same triangle and relabel: notice opposite and adjacent SWAP places while the hypotenuse stays put.
Repeat on a triangle drawn rotated out of standard orientation, labelling relative to θ rather than to the shape.
If a draggable θ marker is available, drag θ between the two acute vertices and watch the opposite/adjacent labels re-attach and swap live while the hypotenuse label stays fixed.
activities.insight: Opposite and adjacent are not glued to the shape; they depend on which angle you are working from. Only the hypotenuse is fixed by the right angle.

activities.title: The ratio that refuses to change (similarity before the mnemonic)
steps: Keep the angle θ fixed and scale a right-angled triangle bigger and smaller (nested similar triangles).
For each size, measure or read opposite and hypotenuse and compute opposite÷hypotenuse; record the values in a table.
Confirm the ratio stays constant (for example 0.42 at every size when θ = 25°) even though the side lengths all change.
Connect this constant to a unit-circle inset: it is named sin θ (with sin θ as the y-coordinate and cos θ as the x-coordinate of the rotating radius).
If a live-scaling model is available, drag to resize the triangle and watch a readout of opp÷hyp stay fixed while the lengths change, with the unit-circle inset naming the constant.
activities.insight: For a given angle the ratio of two sides is invariant regardless of the triangle's size, and that constant value IS sin/cos/tan of the angle — so the ratio has meaning, not just letters.

activities.title: Choose the ratio, then solve for a side or an angle
steps: Given a problem, identify the two sides involved — one known, one unknown — relative to the marked angle θ.
Choose the single ratio (SOH, CAH or TOA) that contains exactly those two sides.
For an unknown SIDE: rearrange the ratio to make the unknown the subject, e.g. from sin 35° = o/10 derive o = 10 × sin 35° ≈ 5.74 cm. (Check: the opposite side cannot exceed the hypotenuse.)
For an unknown ANGLE: apply the inverse function, e.g. from tan θ = 6/8 (opposite 6, adjacent 8) derive θ = tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9°. (Check: an acute angle lies between 0° and 90°.)
Practise a worked case where adjacent and hypotenuse are known: use cosine, θ = cos⁻¹(adjacent/hypotenuse).
If a guided problem mode is available, let it highlight the two relevant sides and branch between 'find a side' (rearrange) and 'find the angle' (inverse).
activities.insight: Ratio selection follows from the pair of sides involved; and whether you rearrange or invert depends on whether the unknown is a side or an angle.

activities.title: Check and discriminate (fixed-step assessment)
steps: Match 'opposite', 'adjacent' and 'hypotenuse' to a triangle with θ marked; then re-answer with θ on the OTHER acute angle to show the swap.
Given two sides, select which ratio applies.
Fill in the blank to compute an unknown side from a known angle.
Fill in the blank using the inverse function (e.g. tan⁻¹) to find an unknown angle.
Include at least one rotated (non-standard orientation) triangle among the items.
activities.insight: Confirm that labels anchor to the reference angle, the correct ratio is chosen for a given side pair, and side-vs-angle problems are finished correctly.

checkQuestion: Give the pupil right-angled triangles with a reference angle θ marked (draw at least one rotated out of standard orientation), and set four tasks to WATCH — do not explain first: (1) On a triangle with θ marked, label the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse; then, on the SAME triangle, mark the other acute angle and label opposite and adjacent for THAT angle. (2) A triangle has θ=35° and hypotenuse 10 cm — find the side opposite θ. (3) A triangle has the two shorter sides 6 cm (opposite) and 8 cm (adjacent) — find angle θ. (4) A triangle gives you the adjacent side and the hypotenuse and asks for the angle — which ratio do you use, and how do you finish? Watch how they label relative to the angle, which ratio they pick, and whether they rearrange or use an inverse.
checkAnswer: (1) Opposite = across from θ, adjacent = next to θ, hypotenuse = opposite the right angle; when the reference angle switches to the other acute angle, opposite and adjacent SWAP while the hypotenuse is unchanged. (2) sin35° = o/10, so o = 10×sin35° ≈ 5.74 cm (rearrange the ratio). (3) tanθ = 6/8, so θ = tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9° (inverse function). (4) Adjacent and hypotenuse → cosine; θ = cos⁻¹(adjacent/hypotenuse).
